question: Describe this Short as a pattern, not its words; quote nothing longer than 6 words. 1) First 3 seconds: what is seen and heard from 0 to 1 s and from 1 to 3 s, when the first spoken word starts, and any on-screen text (how big against the frame, where). 2) Cut rhythm: every cut or shot change with its timestamp, then the count and the average seconds between cuts. 3) On-screen text: word-by-word captions, a title bar, cards or lists; how many words show at once; where on screen. 4) Structure as ordered beats with timestamps, each 12 words or fewer, paraphrased; mark where the main payoff lands (timestamp) and what it is. 5) The end: how it ends (a question to the viewer, a rule, a pitch, a loop back to the start) and what happens in the last 3 seconds. 6) Length, and the speaking pace in words per minute (estimate). 7) The opening move in one line (the kind of line or picture, not the words). 8) The one thing a viewer would forward, and to whom. 9) Every number or claim stated, paraphrased, and whether it names a source. 10) What carries the picture, with a rough share of the runtime: a person on camera, drawn or animated scenes, AI-made images or video, stock or real footage, game footage, text on screen only. 11) How the dispute is staged: who speaks (one narrator, acted voices, a text-to-speech voice), whether each side gets lines, and how the two sides are shown. 12) What changes on screen in the middle third to keep it moving, and the longest stretch with no visual change (seconds).
